newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt firms further in wake of Yeltsin op.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt firms further in wake of Yeltsin op.

text.p: Russian debt added to early gains on news President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation had been completed.
"It is Yeltsin, that is all you need to know," said a trader.
Russian dollar denominated Vneshekonombank debt was up two and a half points from New York's close at 78 3/8 percent of face value by 1142 GMT.

Traders said that there had been some client buying of Russian debt ahead of the operation after a series of deals in the past week which had seen buying of 30 day options as investors sought some exposure to Russia at a lower risk premium than that of holding vnesh directly.
"That deal risk has now disappeared," said a trader.
He expects Vnesh to retest its year highs of over 80 percent of face value as Russia's eurobond roadshow starts in London next week.
"There are some traders taking profits after the gains, but I see Vnesh going to the mid-80s in the longer term," he said.
The market will look over the coming weeks for news that Yeltsin has completely recovered from the operation and will be fit enough to resume the reins of power completely.

Outside of Russia, interest was limited, although Bulgarian debt rose strongly on reports a currency board has been established, which will see the lev pegged to a major currency and thus reduce the risk of holding Bulgarian assets.
Bulgarian IABs were quoted up half a point at 46 bid.
Latin assets were little changed in the wake of a rally in New York. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
